question: The hairy cell leukemia (hairy cell leukemia) presents as characteristic clinical-biological features:

options.opa: Lymphocytosis in peripheral blood greater than 50,000 lymphocytes / microL.
options.opc: Exfoliative generalized erythroderma, plaques and skin tumors.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "characteristic lymphocytosis" -> "peripheral blood lymphocyte count > 50,000 / microL" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "presence of T lymphoid line markers" -> "diagnostic confirmation" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "exfoliative generalized erythroderma" -> "not typical for hairy cell leukemia" -> "possible misdiagnosis" -> 60%
analysis: Hairy cell leukemia is characterized by pancytopenia and splenomegaly, which are common findings in this condition due to the infiltration of the bone marrow and spleen by hairy cells. Lymphocytosis is not typically greater than 50,000 lymphocytes/microL, and T lymphoid line markers are not characteristic of hairy cell leukemia, which is a B-cell neoplasm. Exfoliative generalized erythroderma and skin tumors are not associated with hairy cell leukemia.
